newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares endend Monday's trade steadier with industrials softening after early gains on the back of Friday's stronger Wall Street and golds heeding bullion's slight recoveries, dealers said.
"It has been a relatively quiet trading day," James Scott, an equities trader at stockbroking firm Societe Generale Frankel Pollack told Reuters.
He said the market's sentiment was cautious to bullish, but market players were awaiting cues from some of this week's economic indicators due for release.
Indicators due out are March consumer price and March trade figures on Wednesday and March M3 money supply and private credit growth on Thursday.

"We have a reasonably firmer undertone on the market following through Wall Street's gains on Friday. We've seen some good offshore and local demand for our shares through last week which I think followed through today," Scott added.

The industrial shares perked up sligthly early on Monday following Wall Street's Friday's gains, but softened in the afternoon with dealers saying market players saw New York's correction as not yet over.
"Many people see Friday's (gains) on Wall Street as a slightly false market," one dealer said.
The industrial index closed 22.5 points up at 8,338, the all-share ended up 17.8 points to 7,040 and the gold index gained 9.9 points to finish at 1,257.6.

Dealers said volumes had been moderate with 650 million rand worth of shares traded, while the bourse's financial index reached a new all time high of 8,695 compared with a previous record of 8,678 on March 13.

Golds were firmer on the back of a sligthly recovered bullion price, but a firmer rand held back real advances, Scott said, adding the market had already discounted most of the poor gold quarterly results released last week and some still due later this week.
Bullion stood at around $342 an ounce on Monday after trading below $340 an ounce last week.
Tuesday's trade was expected to be unchanged, dealers said, adding among Monday's star attractions had been Malbak which saw a corporate finance deal of about 3.3 million rand worth of shares.
"I see a continued steady to firmer market," Scott said.
Dealers said among the subdued stocks on Monday had been De Beers which shed 125 cents to 158.75 rand and Anglo which added 50 cents to close at 281.75 rand.
Dealers said market players were taking a wait and see attitude in order to carefully study last week's news that the long awaited agreement between De Beers and Russia could be signed soon.
The agreement, which has been stalled for months over some legal nuances, will allow De Beers' Central Selling Organisation to sell Russia's diamonds on the world's markets.

They said the slight disinterest in Anglo stemmed from Wednesday's announcement by Zairean rebels that they had signed a $1 billion deal with Canada's America Mineral Fields before the minging house and other international companies, who had also tendered to develop the Kolwezi copper/cobalt tailings in Lubumbashi.
Near-dated stock futures were also steady towards close with industrial futures receiving slight cheers from Friday's close of Wall Street and golds taking note of bullion's steady climb.
The June industrial contract was at 8,145/53 from 8,180 settlement, all-share was at 6,500/10 from 6,519 and the golds contract were at 885/91 from 878.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
